study.title: James 4: desires at war, humility before God and practical obedience
study.overview: James 4 denounces that disputes among believers are not born, first of all, of external causes, but of disorderly desires that dominate the interior. The chapter calls the reader to abandon friendship with the world, submit to God, resist the devil, repent with sincerity, curb the tongue, recognize divine sovereignty over the future and act according to the well-known. The message is profoundly practical: true piety appears not only in correct words, but in humility, purity, prayer, mercy, and obedience.

outline.title: Wars are born of disorderly desires
outline.explanation: James asks for the origin of the fights and points to the greedy that warn within the person. The text shows that external violence is the result of an inner conflict, and even prayer can be corrupted when it is asked only to feed selfish pleasures.

outline.title: Friendship with the world, jealousy of God and grace to the humble
outline.explanation: Language is severe: seeking intimacy with the system of values opposite God is spiritual infidelity. Still, James highlights divine mercy: God gives greater grace to the humble and opposes the proud.

outline.title: Submission to God, Repentance and Dominion of the Language
outline.explanation: The call is double: to submit to God and to resist the devil, approaching the Lord with hands and hearts cleansed. Then James condemns the evil speech and the arrogant judgment of the brother, remembering that there is one Legislator and Judge.

outline.title: humble planning and sin of omission
outline.explanation: James rebukes self-confidence in business and plans for the future, for life is brief and depends on the will of the Lord. The chapter ends with a decisive principle: knowing how to do good and not doing it is already sin.

study.context: The notes indicate that James speaks to Christians marked by internal and external conflicts. There is reference to itinerant merchant practices that trusted in their own initiative to overcome poverty and low social condition, and also to the tension generated by material desires, pride and rivalries. The picture of the notes is that of a community in which faith was being affected by ambition, destructive speech and presumption about the future.
study.theology: James 4 presents an integrated moral and spiritual vision. Sin is not only an isolated act, but a desire that governs the heart and contaminates relationships, prayers, and decisions. The chapter teaches that friendship with the world is incompatible with fidelity to God, but also that divine grace is greater than human pride. The correct answer to sin includes submission, resistance to the devil, visible repentance, humility and confidence in providence. Moreover, James states that God is the only Lawgiver and Judge, which severely limits the accuser spirit among brethren. The chapter culminates in an ethics of responsibility: it is not enough to know the good; it is necessary to practice it. Thus, conscious omission is treated as real sin.

scholarViews.insight: James describes the quarrels as the fruit of evil desires in war within people, and connects this same source also to prayer without answer.
The evil speech against the brother is condemned because it must be guided by the law of goodness, not only by the naked and raw truth.
Those who know good and do not do it assume greater guilt, for ignorance cannot be claimed after the warning received.

questions: What internal desires are fueling conflicts, anxiety or impatience in my life today?
Has my prayer been seeking the will of God or just the satisfaction of my pleasures?
In which area I already know what is right, but have I postponed obeying?
study.practice: This week, practice three concrete attitudes: first, sincerely examine what desires have governed their reactions and confess this to God; secondly, before talking about someone, ask if their words will build or injure; third, when making plans, consciously add the submission to the will of the Lord. Also choose a clear opportunity to do good to someone and not postpone this action.
study.uncertainty: The notes do not clarify with certainty whether James quotes here a specific biblical phrase in 5, nor allow to safely identify the exact source of the expression mentioned in 4:5; therefore, the meaning was treated with caution. It is also not possible to confirm on the basis of the notes only the full historical scenario of the chapter, only the explicitly suggested elements: conflicts between readers, material ambition and presumption about the future.
